scenes.line1: How does Airflow handle missed runs?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how Airflow deals with missed runs and historical data? Let’s break down scheduling, data intervals, catchup, and backfill.

scenes.label: Interval
scenes.sub: schedule_interval controls when your DAG runs.
scenes.say: Airflow uses the schedule interval to decide when your workflow, or DAG, should run. You set it with cron or timedelta.

rows.b: Each run covers a time period

scenes.say: Each DAG run covers a data interval—a logical window, not the actual runtime. This helps partition and organize your data.
Catchup lets Airflow run all missed intervals since the DAG’s start date. Backfill is the process of running those historical periods, either automatically or manually.

scenes.question: What happens if catchup=False?
scenes.right: Airflow only runs the latest scheduled interval and skips missed runs, preventing overload.
scenes.say: If you set catchup to false, Airflow skips all missed runs and only schedules the latest interval. This avoids accidental overload.
